title: The Pluperfect Subjunctive: Hubiera and Hubiese + Participle

sections.title: What you know
sections.content: You know *hubiera* + a past participle from B1 Unit 35, where it imagines a past that did not happen (*Si hubiera tenido tiempo*). You also know it in the result clause and without *si* from B2 Unit 10 (*Hubiera salido antes, habría llegado*). This lesson puts the form itself in order: all the persons, the two variants *hubiera* and *hubiese*, and the places where you will meet it.

sections.title: Two variants, one meaning
sections.content: *Hubiera* and *hubiese* are the two imperfect subjunctive forms of *haber*, with the same *-ra* and *-se* endings as in B2 Unit 15. Each is followed by a past participle, which never changes: *hubiera salido*, *hubiese salido*. The two variants mean exactly the same. In Latin America *hubiera* is by far the commoner; *hubiese* is mostly something you read.

sections.title: Hubiera and hubiese + participle (salir)
rows: él, ella, usted hubiera / hubiese salido
ellos, ellas, ustedes hubieran / hubiesen salido

items.spanish: Si hubiéramos salido antes, habríamos llegado a tiempo.
items.english: If we had left earlier, we would have arrived on time.

items.spanish: Si lo hubiese sabido, te habría llamado.
items.english: If I had known, I would have called you.

items.spanish: Hubiera dicho la verdad, nadie se habría molestado.
items.english: Had he told the truth, nobody would have been upset.

items.spanish: No creía que hubieran terminado tan pronto.
items.english: I did not think they had finished so soon.

sections.content: The participle never changes for gender or number: *hubieran terminado*, not *hubieran terminados*. Object pronouns go before *hubiera*: *si lo hubiera sabido*, *si me hubieras avisado*. *Hubiéramos* and *hubiésemos* always carry an accent. After a verb of doubt or feeling in the past, *hubiera* + participle says that the thing happened before: you will practise this in lesson 4.
